answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to post a quartz-backed bond that unlocks only after a long record of honest, verifiable work. A random audit, swift as a zephyr, periodically checks that the agent still controls that single record; a copy cannot share it. An attacker who plants many fake identities must therefore fund and age a separate bond for each one, like growing a walnut tree from seed for every copy, while an honest agent pays once and reuses its history, so mass forgery stops paying.
